newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean police inspect German colony.
newsitem.headline: Chilean police inspect German colony.

text.p: A convoy of Chilean police inspected a secretive German colony in southern Chile on Wednesday for the fifth time in eight days in search of its founder, wanted on child-molesting and other charges.

Witnesses said a line of police vans and trucks entered Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony) near the town of Parral and left a few hours later for the latest in a series of what police called "visual inspections" of the German-speaking enclave.
The inspections, carried out with a judge's permission, were basically spy missions that could be the first step to a raid on the settlement, Chilean news reports said.

Police made no arrests and met no obvious resistance from the followers of Paul Schaeffer, who founded the settlement in the early 1960s and faces a long list of charges including molesting Chilean boys sent to a boarding school inside the colony.
Though peaceful, the police inspections alarmed the community's 300-some German residents and raised tension at the settlement as never before in its nearly 40 years of existence.
President Eduardo Frei said this week that the colony, viewed in the government as an anomaly that hurts Chile's image abroad, could no longer exist as it has on the margins of Chilean law.
"We cannot continue to allow that in the case of the ex-Colonia Dignidad, people to continue to live as they have for the past 36 years," Frei said Monday.

Santiago news reports said on Wednesday that the colony had begun buying up land in Paraguay and Brazil with which to set up another community if they were expelled from Chile and if legal pressures grew too great.
Followers say Schaefer, a corporal in the Nazi army in World War II, has not been seen in the colony for about seven months but they would not say where he is.

He has many supporters among big local landowners, who share his right-wing ideology, and peasants who are allowed to use the colony's modern hospital, and media speculated he could be hiding with friends.
Groups of candle-bearing peasants held vigils in support of the elderly Schaefer outside the colony in recent days.
